usage:a-little-bit.title: a little bit：有一点、稍微
usage:a-little-bit.explanation: 程度副词，表示“略微、一点点”，用于弱化语气、让表达更柔和口语化，常修饰形容词、动词或不可数名词。口语高频；书面正式表达更常用 a little / slightly。
usage:a-little-bit.source: We'll talk about that a little bit later on.
usage:a-little-bit.example: I'm a little bit tired today. / 我今天有点累。

usage:after-不宜直接当-later-连接后续动作.id: usage:after-不宜直接当-later-连接后续动作
usage:after-不宜直接当-later-连接后续动作.title: after 不宜直接当 later 连接后续动作
usage:after-不宜直接当-later-连接后续动作.explanation: 表达“后来……”时，after 不能直接替代 later/then/afterward 来承接后续动作；自然说法是 but later settled 或 but then settled。
usage:after-不宜直接当-later-连接后续动作.source: 表达“后来……”时，after 不能直接替代 later/then/afterward 来承接后续动作；自然说法是 but later settled 或 but then settled。

usage:all-set-register.title: all set 的语气与场景
usage:all-set-register.explanation: 偏口语、亲切安抚的语气，美式英语高频。常见于餐厅点餐后服务员问 Are you all set?（点好了吗）、出发前确认 All set?、以及向对方保证 All set—we've taken care of everything。比 ready 更口语、更有人情味。
usage:all-set-register.example: All set! The tickets are booked and the bags are packed. / Don't worry, everything's all set for the meeting.

usage:back-east-in-the-east-eastward-con.title: back east、in the East 与 eastward 的区别
usage:back-east-in-the-east-eastward-con.explanation: back east 带有从当前所在地回望美国东部原居地或熟悉地区的意味；in the East 只客观说明位于某个东部地区；eastward 强调朝东的移动或方向，通常不表达故乡联系。
usage:back-east-in-the-east-eastward-con.example: After living in California for years, she traveled eastward to visit her family back east.

usage:cannot-vs-cant.title: cannot 与 can't 的语域差异
usage:cannot-vs-cant.explanation: cannot 更正式，书面语与强调句中常用；can't 是口语缩略，日常对话更自然。
usage:cannot-vs-cant.source: I cannot stand the smell of smoke.
usage:cannot-vs-cant.example: I cannot (can't) stand waiting in line.

usage:continue-continue-on-proceed-regis.title: continue、continue on 与 proceed 的语域差异
usage:continue-continue-on-proceed-regis.explanation: continue 最通用，可表示继续动作或状态；continue on 强调沿当前路线或方向继续；proceed 更正式，常见于交通指示、公告和流程说明。
usage:continue-continue-on-proceed-regis.example: When the light turns green, proceed through the intersection carefully.

usage:dish-out-criticism-punishment-nega.title: dish out 批评或惩罚时的语气
usage:dish-out-criticism-punishment-nega.explanation: dish out 用在 criticism、punishment、insults 等词前时，常带有“不断给出、强硬施加”的语气；短语 can dish it out but cannot take it 表示一个人会批评别人却受不了别人批评自己。
usage:dish-out-criticism-punishment-nega.source: dish out criticism / can dish it out but cannot take it
usage:dish-out-criticism-punishment-nega.example: He can dish out criticism, but he gets upset when others criticize him.

usage:dish-up-vs-dish-out-food-vs-distri.title: dish up 与 dish out 的语义区别
usage:dish-up-vs-dish-out-food-vs-distri.explanation: dish up 更强调把饭菜盛好、端上桌这个餐桌动作；dish out 更强调把东西一个个分出去，语义范围更宽，也常带有批评、惩罚等抽象含义。
usage:dish-up-vs-dish-out-food-vs-distri.example: She dished up the stew, while he dished out napkins to everyone.

usage:dish-up-vs-serve-food.title: dish up 和 serve 的区别
usage:dish-up-vs-serve-food.explanation: dish up 强调把食物从锅或大盘里盛到盘子/碗里的动作，语气更日常；serve 范围更宽，既可以指端菜、上菜，也可以指餐厅服务或正式待客。
usage:dish-up-vs-serve-food.example: My dad dished up the rice, and my sister served the drinks.

usage:dish-up-word-order-object-position.title: dish up 的宾语位置
usage:dish-up-word-order-object-position.explanation: dish up 是可分短语动词，名词宾语可以放在 up 前后，如 dish up the rice 或 dish the rice up；代词宾语通常放中间，如 dish it up。
usage:dish-up-word-order-object-position.example: Could you dish it up while I set the table?

usage:drizzle-vs-rain-shower.title: drizzle、rain 和 shower 的语感区别
usage:drizzle-vs-rain-shower.explanation: drizzle 强调雨很细很轻；rain 是最普通的下雨说法；shower 常指短时间的一阵雨。描述天气时，drizzle 往往带有潮湿、灰蒙蒙、轻微但持续的感觉。
usage:drizzle-vs-rain-shower.example: There was a light drizzle all morning. 整个早上都下着小毛毛雨。

usage:first-then-action-sequence.title: first, then 表示动作顺序
usage:first-then-action-sequence.explanation: first, then 用来清楚安排两个先后动作，适合做饭、计划、说明步骤等场景；first 放在第一个动作后或句首都可以，then 引出下一步。
usage:first-then-action-sequence.source: Sure. I’ll slice the bread first, then pour the juice.
usage:first-then-action-sequence.example: I’ll wash the vegetables first, then chop them.

usage:go-for-it-vs-go-ahead.title: go for it 与 go ahead 的语气差异
usage:go-for-it-vs-go-ahead.explanation: go for it 是口语打气语，带朋友间的温度与鼓励，偏“加油、去争取”；go ahead 更像“批准/允许”，回答别人请示时用，意思是“可以，去吧”。正式书面场合一般不用 go for it。
usage:go-for-it-vs-go-ahead.example: A: I'm nervous about the audition. B: Don't be — go for it!

usage:lovely-day-comment-suggestion.title: Lovely day to...：用天气引出建议或感叹
usage:lovely-day-comment-suggestion.explanation: Lovely day to... 字面是在评价天气，实际常带有轻松的建议、邀请或感叹意味，相当于说‘天气这么好，很适合……’。这种说法自然、友好，偏日常口语。
usage:lovely-day-comment-suggestion.example: Lovely day to eat outside, isn't it?

usage:may-proceed-traffic-permission.title: 交通语境中的 may proceed
usage:may-proceed-traffic-permission.explanation: 说明交通信号给予通行许可时，may proceed 比 can continue on 更精确，并隐含确认道路安全后再通行。
usage:may-proceed-traffic-permission.source: A green light on a traffic signal means your car can continue on
usage:may-proceed-traffic-permission.example: When the light turns green, you may proceed if the intersection is clear.

usage:now-as-discourse-marker-explanatio.title: Now 用作讲解开场
usage:now-as-discourse-marker-explanatio.explanation: 句首 Now 可以不是时间副词“现在”，而是话语标记，用来把听者注意力拉到接下来要解释的内容上，语气像“那么/注意”。
usage:now-as-discourse-marker-explanatio.source: Now, to dish up something means...
usage:now-as-discourse-marker-explanatio.example: Now, this expression is usually used in casual conversation.

usage:pit-stop-informal-register.title: make a pit stop 为口语非正式表达
usage:pit-stop-informal-register.explanation: 语气轻松、偏口语，适合朋友、家人或熟悉同事之间；较正式的场合可改说 take a short break 或 stop briefly。
usage:pit-stop-informal-register.source: Do you think we can make a pit stop?
usage:pit-stop-informal-register.example: 正式场合：We may take a short break.（口语：Can we make a pit stop?）

usage:pretty-as-adverb-informal.title: pretty as an informal intensifier
usage:pretty-as-adverb-informal.explanation: In informal spoken American English, 'pretty' acts as an adverb meaning 'fairly, quite, rather' before an adjective or adverb (pretty big, pretty good, pretty fast). It softens the claim rather than strongly amplifying it. Best avoided in formal academic or business writing; use 'quite' or 'rather' there.
usage:pretty-as-adverb-informal.source: a pretty big price to pay
usage:pretty-as-adverb-informal.example: The movie was pretty good, but the ending disappointed me.

usage:reassure-prepared-tone.title: 用 got ... covered 表达安抚、宽慰语气
usage:reassure-prepared-tone.explanation: 该表达带宽慰语气，强调「已安排妥当、可放心」。常用于团队分工、活动筹备等非正式场合；正式书面可用 has been taken care of / has been handled 替代。
usage:reassure-prepared-tone.example: Relax, the whole itinerary is covered. 放心，整个行程都安排好了。

usage:serve-food-and-drinks-kitchen-cont.title: serve：端上或供应食物饮料
usage:serve-food-and-drinks-kitchen-cont.explanation: 厨房和餐桌语境里，serve 表示把饭菜或饮料提供给别人，可以是端上桌、分给客人，也可以表示餐厅或酒店供应某种食物。
usage:serve-food-and-drinks-kitchen-cont.example: Serve the soup with fresh bread.

usage:serve-food-broad-use.title: serve food 的宽泛用法
usage:serve-food-broad-use.explanation: serve food 不一定说明食物已经被盛到个人盘子里，它可以表示上菜、提供食物、招待客人，语域比 dish up 更中性，也更适合正式场景。
usage:serve-food-broad-use.example: The hotel serves breakfast from seven to ten.

usage:shall-we-suggestion-friendly.title: Shall we...?：友好地提出建议
usage:shall-we-suggestion-friendly.explanation: Shall we...? 常用于邀请对方一起做某事，语气礼貌、轻松，尤其适合共同活动。它比 Do you want to...? 稍微更优雅一点。
usage:shall-we-suggestion-friendly.source: Shall we take the boat out?
usage:shall-we-suggestion-friendly.example: Shall we sit outside for lunch?

usage:should-not-for-negative-expectatio.title: shouldn't：表示预计某事不会发生
usage:should-not-for-negative-expectatio.explanation: shouldn't + 动词除了可以表示不应该做某事，还可以根据上下文表达说话人的判断：按目前情况看，某事预计不会发生。This drizzle shouldn't cause much trouble 表示说话人预计这点毛毛雨不会造成太大麻烦，并非在谈义务或禁止。
usage:should-not-for-negative-expectatio.source: This drizzle shouldn't cause much trouble.
usage:should-not-for-negative-expectatio.example: The delay shouldn't affect our plans.

usage:stand-vs-bear-putupwith.title: stand / bear / put up with / tolerate 近义辨析
usage:stand-vs-bear-putupwith.explanation: stand 表“忍受”几乎只用于否定或疑问句；bear 语气更强、更书面；put up with 口语化、表“容忍”；tolerate 最正式。肯定句中要表达“忍受”时优先用 bear 或 put up with。
usage:stand-vs-bear-putupwith.source: I cannot stand the smell of smoke.
usage:stand-vs-bear-putupwith.example: How can you put up with that noise every day?
